image_prompt.text: Painted sidelines and baselines marking the edge of the blacktop court
A centre circle at midcourt and free-throw spots the ball is put back into play from
A backboard, rim and net on a pole at each end of the court
Painted three-point arc, key and free-throw line on the asphalt
Chain-link fencing enclosing the court so the ball stays in
An open blacktop area around the court where players gather between games
the city park the court sits in — grass, trees, benches and street lamps around the blacktop

layout_placement.text: A detection perimeter on the court lines so play stops the moment the ball or a player crosses out
Fixed reset positions at midcourt and the free-throw line for restarting play
An invisible cylinder through each hoop that registers a made basket

notes: Preset Court Sport taken whole; added barrier-perimeter, marker-distance and social-hub for the street-court and park half of the reference.
social-hub taken from options.md, where it is listed as worded by '6 genres' and no genre is named — text written from the prompt instead of a genre's wording.
trigger-scoring emitted as `both` per Sports' own table; options.md lists the same ID as `layout` only.
marker-distance is not in the Court Sport preset; added because a basketball court's three-point arc and key are constitutive markings rather than decoration.
Built as one court. NBA 2K's Park is several adjacent courts; the prompt says 'court' singular, so the multi-court reading is an open question.
The run ends at the hoop — inferred from the genre per step 4, not asked.

Should it read as a gritty real-world city park — cracked asphalt, chain-link, graffiti — or as a bright stylized Roblox look with clean saturated colours?

skill_gap.name: no rule for expanding a named reference
skill_gap.why: the entire prompt is a reference to a commercial game's mode, and how much of it to build — one court, or the multi-court social park it names — changes the shape, the scale band and half the options. The only guidance anywhere in the skills is a single example row ('an exact replica of the Blox Fruits first sea') in the mixing table, which shows a reference being read for genre but says nothing about how far to expand one into geometry.

notes_for_us: options.md gives `social-hub` as worded by '6 genres' and names none, so step 2's instruction to 'say which genre you took it from' cannot be followed and there is no genre wording to inject.
`trigger-scoring` is `both` in sports.md but `layout` in options.md, while options.md states the route and Goes to 'come with the row' — the two files contradict on a Core option.
layout-intake gives `scale` an `assumed` flag but theme none, so a theme inferred from a reference is indistinguishable downstream from one the user stated.
Sports has no row for the grounds a facility sits in: `space-bounded` is the court perimeter and `barrier-perimeter` is the fence, so the surrounding park had nowhere to go but free text.
prompts.json for this run has no `enriched` field, so `coverage.enriched_invented` could not be filled as LANE-BRIEF describes.
